_: The settings of ONE model of this mod - the accurate one. This file is PRIVATE to this mod. It used to be the interface: when a model mod was a data file, the adapter itself parsed it, and that is why the old version could carry no address and no program. A model mod is a shim now, the contract is the C ABI in speechbroker-voice-model.h, and nothing outside SpeechBrokerModelWhisperRu.dll reads this file. The shim writes this file out of its built-in values the first time it finds none, so deleting it is safe and deleting one line of it is safe too.
name: Whisper large-v3-turbo, Russian
_language: What the model LISTENS in, ISO 639-1. The adapter logs it and routes nothing on it at contract version 1.
_provides: The adapter knows only 'asr' at contract version 1. It used to say 'asr,tts' here, which was false about Whisper: Whisper does not speak. Speech is a model mod of its own, and it did not go missing - it was always a separate thing.
_class: 'fast' or 'accurate'. A HINT, and the only thing it decides is whether this model is asked on an INTERIM pass; the final pass of every turn asks everybody. The adapter replaces it with a measured p90 once it has five latency samples, and latencies are not carried between runs, so this declaration is the interim roster at the start of every session.
_finalOnly: BINDING, not a hint, and the one declaration measurement does not override - it is about cost, not speed. False here because this model is on this machine and a pass costs a memcpy. A model across a network should say true.
_budgetMs: How long this model asks to be given for a final pass. For the first five passes of a session the deadline IS this plus a slack of 1000 ms; under-declare and those passes close underneath you and are counted against your standing. Declare what can actually be met.
_startupMs: How long Start may take, and how long the adapter waits between attempts. It tries five times. Loading large-v3-turbo off a cold disk is the case this number is for.
_stopMs: How long Stop may take, and it is deliberately NOT startupMs: one of the two moments Stop is called is the moment the player wants out of the game, and a minute of that is the difference between a build that can be edited afterwards and one that cannot.
_maxInFlight: How many utterances this model can hold at once. Read by the adapter against the debt, so a true number means BUSY is never answered at all.
_weights: Relative to the folder this file is in, and it may not leave it. The weights, the SHA256SUMS beside them and the archive a player installs are one unit: a path leading out of the mod means the thing that was verified and the thing that was shipped are not the same thing.
_requireSums: Refuse to start when there is no SHA256SUMS beside the weights, rather than only when it does not match. Measured: five hundred flipped bytes inside a converted model produce no error anywhere and a model that answers rubbish, and nothing above this line can tell that from a hard accent. Turn it off while building a model mod of your own, before the sums exist.

child._: How the child process is raised and what it is told. Every path here is relative to the folder of this file and may not leave it.
child._library: The backend, loaded by the child by FULL PATH at run time. It is not linked: linking would make the child refuse to start with an unreadable loader error instead of one sentence naming the file that is missing.
child._preload: Dependencies of that library, loaded by full path IN ORDER before it. This list is why nothing here ever touches PATH or SetDefaultDllDirectories - a bare-name load later finds an already-loaded module without any policy change at all.
child._promptPhrases: How many of the adapter's vocabulary phrases to keep as a prompt. The reference kept 40: an initial prompt competes for a window that also has to hold the answer, and a long one makes recognition worse.
